transactions.title: The name is called in Charlotte.
transactions.text: Charlotte selects Kobe Bryant at No. 13. The draft selection and the eventual rights transfer have different effective dates.

transactions.title: Thirteen becomes a Laker.
transactions.shortTitle: Kobe’s rights go to Los Angeles
transactions.text: Los Angeles sends Vlade Divac to Charlotte for Bryant’s draft rights. A straight exchange with a long basketball afterlife.
notes: Charlotte’s official historical record lists July 11 as the rights trade date. This story ends at the transfer; later free agency is not drawn as a trade return.

transactions.title: Dallas bets on the unknown.
transactions.text: The Mavericks exchange No. 6 for two sets of draft rights. One belongs to Dirk. The other is already headed into another deal.

transactions.title: The other half of draft night.
transactions.text: Garrity’s rights join two players and a future first. Phoenix sends Steve Nash to Dallas in a separate exchange.

transactions.title: No. 9: Shawn Marion
transactions.text: The first Dallas sent for Nash becomes Phoenix’s No. 9 selection: Shawn Marion.

transactions.title: The dynasty splits.
transactions.text: Shaq leaves Los Angeles. One player in Miami’s return package, Caron Butler, will later join another exchange.
notes: The Lakers’ historical guide also records Miami’s 2007 second-round pick; it is included alongside the better-known 2006 first.

transactions.title: A bridge named Caron Butler.
transactions.text: Butler and Atkins go to Washington. Brown and Profit move to Los Angeles. The bridge runs through a package, not Butler alone.
notes: The Wizards page carries a July 29 publication date; the completed sign-and-trade took effect August 2.

transactions.title: No. 26: Jordan Farmar
transactions.text: Miami’s first becomes No. 26. The Lakers select Jordan Farmar.

transactions.title: The second takes a Dallas detour.
transactions.text: Dallas sends Pinnock’s draft rights to Los Angeles. The Miami second from the Shaq package goes the other way.

transactions.title: No. 50: Renaldas Seibutis
transactions.text: Dallas uses the Miami-origin second at No. 50 on Renaldas Seibutis. This branch ends with his draft rights.

transactions.title: Boston goes all in.
transactions.text: Five players, a Boston first, a returned Minnesota obligation and cash go west. Garnett joins Boston, then becomes part of the 2013 Brooklyn package.

resolutions.detail: Returned to Minnesota: Boston relinquishes the prior claim on Minnesota’s own conditional first.

transactions.title: One Gasol for another.
transactions.text: Pau heads to Los Angeles. Memphis receives a package containing his younger brother’s draft rights, three players and two firsts.
notes: Marc is represented as draft rights at this moment. Cash and the Memphis second-round pick are part of the exchange, even though they rarely make the headline.

transactions.title: Two old branches cross.
transactions.text: Shaq goes to Phoenix. Marion, selected with the Dallas first from the Nash exchange, moves to Miami with Banks.

transactions.title: The same two players move again.
transactions.shortTitle: Marion and Banks go to Toronto
transactions.text: Marion and Banks go to Toronto. Miami receives Jermaine O’Neal, Moon and conditional draft consideration.
notes: Miami generated a reported $4.2 million traded-player exception. An exception is cap capacity created by a transaction; it is not a player or pick transferred from another team.
Toronto’s first-round obligation is not followed further. Reports disagree on final-year protection wording; the known 2010 lottery protection and separate conditional second are retained.

transactions.title: Another stop for the Big Fella.
transactions.text: Cleveland acquires Shaq. Wallace, Pavlović, a second and cash go to Phoenix.

transactions.title: The Dallas pick comes home.
transactions.text: Marion reaches Dallas through a four-team sign-and-trade. The 1999 pick’s path has passed through Phoenix, Miami and Toronto.
notes: Marion and Türkoğlu were signed and traded. Cash directions follow the team media guides; amounts are not asserted.
Orlando also created a traded-player exception. This is generated cap capacity, not a transferable pick.

transactions.title: Butler’s branch reaches Dallas, too.
transactions.text: Washington sends three players and cash to Dallas. Four players leave the Mavericks in the exchange.

transactions.title: No. 28: Greivis Vásquez
transactions.text: The later Lakers first in the Gasol exchange becomes No. 28. Memphis selects Greivis Vásquez.

transactions.title: A Christmas Eve exchange.
transactions.text: Vásquez goes to New Orleans for Pondexter. Two young players trade places.

transactions.title: A sixth man gets his own team.
transactions.text: Houston acquires Harden with three other players. Oklahoma City takes Martin, Lamb and three pick obligations with very different conditions.

transactions.title: No. 12: Steven Adams
transactions.text: Toronto lands inside the permitted lottery range. Oklahoma City uses No. 12 on Steven Adams.

transactions.title: No. 32: Álex Abrines
transactions.text: The second-round asset in the Harden package becomes the rights to Álex Abrines.

transactions.title: The protection holds.
transactions.text: Dallas’s No. 13 first stays protected. Oklahoma City must wait; this is the same obligation, not an extra pick.

resolutions.detail: Dallas’s 2013 pick is No. 13, inside the protected 1–20 range. The obligation rolls to 2014.

transactions.title: Three teams make room for Evans.
transactions.text: Vásquez moves to Sacramento, Evans to New Orleans, and Lopez to Portland. Draft rights, seconds and cash complete the package.
notes: Evans was signed and traded. The final July 10 transaction is used, not the July 4 agreement. The published team summaries compress the secondary rights into draft consideration; Mark Deeks’s record supplies the two second-round swap rights.

transactions.title: Brooklyn buys the present.
transactions.text: Veterans go to Brooklyn. Boston receives five players, three future firsts and a swap right whose value will take years to emerge.
notes: Keith Bogans was signed and traded. The 2014 first remained subject to Atlanta’s prior swap rights. The conditional Boston second is included separately.

transactions.title: A seven-player reset.
transactions.shortTitle: Vásquez joins the Rudy Gay package
transactions.text: Vásquez moves again, this time to Toronto with three teammates. Gay, Acy and Gray go to Sacramento.

transactions.title: No. 21: Mitch McGary
transactions.text: No. 21 sits just outside the protection. Dallas’s obligation finally conveys.

transactions.title: No. 17: James Young
transactions.text: The first of the three outright Brooklyn obligations settles at No. 17.

transactions.title: One guard. Two separate futures.
transactions.shortTitle: Vásquez for Powell rights and a first
transactions.text: Milwaukee receives Vásquez. Toronto takes Powell’s draft rights and a protected Clippers first.

transactions.title: No. 3: Jaylen Brown
transactions.text: Brooklyn’s 2016 obligation becomes No. 3. Boston selects Jaylen Brown.

transactions.title: The lottery fixes Boston’s position.
transactions.text: May 16 establishes the pick positions: Boston is allocated Brooklyn’s No. 1 through the swap. This is the lottery determination date, not a sourced administrative exercise date.

resolutions.detail: Boston receives Brooklyn’s No. 1; Brooklyn receives Boston’s No. 27. Boston’s No. 57 second-round selection also conveys.

notes: May 16 is the date the lottery established the positions. The swap was exercised for the 2017 draft; this scene records the now-known allocation.

transactions.title: Boston trades down.
transactions.text: The No. 1 selection changes hands again. Boston takes No. 3 and another conditional first-round entitlement.

transactions.title: No. 23: OG Anunoby
transactions.text: The Clippers first conveys at No. 23. Toronto selects OG Anunoby.

transactions.title: The pick becomes Tatum.
transactions.text: Boston selects Jayson Tatum at No. 3. Brooklyn’s swap was one step in this route; Philadelphia’s trade-down deal was another.

transactions.title: A new running mate in Oklahoma.
transactions.text: Indiana trades Paul George for two young players. Two years later, Oklahoma City will send George into another, much larger exchange.

transactions.title: The last Brooklyn first leaves Boston.
transactions.shortTitle: Brooklyn first joins the Kyrie package
transactions.text: Boston includes the 2018 Brooklyn obligation in its Irving package. Cleveland receives three players and two draft assets.
notes: The August 22 proposal was amended. Miami’s 2020 second was added before completion on August 30; the joint announcement was published after midnight UTC.
Irving’s later Boston departure was free agency. This route follows the Brooklyn pick, not an invented trade from Boston to Brooklyn.

transactions.title: Not this lottery.
transactions.text: The Lakers’ pick lands at No. 10. Boston’s entitlement requires No. 2–5, so the same obligation moves to its 2019 comparison.

resolutions.detail: Lakers No. 10 is outside the 2018 conveyance range. The obligation now compares the Sacramento and Philadelphia 2019 firsts under the original terms.

transactions.title: Two picks. Two futures.
transactions.text: Dallas moves up from No. 5 to No. 3. The extra first-round obligation gives Atlanta a second path into the future.
notes: The draft took place June 21 in the United States. The NBA release timestamp is June 22 UTC. These are draft rights, not signed NBA contracts.

transactions.title: No. 8: Collin Sexton
transactions.text: The third outright first from the 2013 Brooklyn trade becomes Cleveland’s No. 8 selection.

transactions.title: Toronto takes the leap.
transactions.text: Leonard and Green go north. San Antonio receives DeRozan, Poeltl and a protected first. Poeltl’s branch will eventually bend back.

transactions.title: The younger brother moves north.
transactions.text: Eleven years after his rights arrived in Memphis, Marc goes to Toronto. Three players and a second-round obligation move the other way.

transactions.title: No. 29: Keldon Johnson
transactions.text: Toronto’s first lands at No. 29, outside the protection. San Antonio selects Keldon Johnson.

transactions.title: No. 14: Romeo Langford
transactions.text: Sacramento’s No. 14 satisfies the conditional entitlement. Boston selects Romeo Langford.

transactions.title: No. 10: Cam Reddish
transactions.text: The protection does not apply at No. 10. Atlanta uses the Dallas selection on Cam Reddish.

transactions.title: Los Angeles makes its move.
transactions.text: Davis goes to Los Angeles in a three-team package. Players, draft rights, future obligations, a swap and cash all move.
notes: The deal became official July 6; the NBA repost is timestamped July 7 UTC. The Hunter rights later entered a separate Atlanta trade, outside this branch.

transactions.title: The price of right now.
transactions.text: George goes to the Clippers. Oklahoma City receives Gilgeous-Alexander, Gallinari, five firsts and two swap rights.
notes: Miami’s 2023 obligation was later amended; the original contract terms are preserved here. Only the 2022 Clippers first is followed to a selection.

transactions.title: Four teams. Two stories intersect.
transactions.shortTitle: Harden, Oladipo and LeVert change teams
transactions.text: Harden goes to Brooklyn. Oladipo, part of Indiana’s Paul George return, enters the same exchange. LeVert goes to Indiana.
notes: January 16 is the completed four-team deal. The January 14 three-team announcement was amended after physicals; this is one final package, not two trades of Harden.
The Cleveland/Utah second was initially slated for Brooklyn, but went to Indiana in the final structure. Net movements are recorded, including Vezenkov’s draft rights and Brooklyn cash.
The 2021 and 2025 swap rights interact with prior Oklahoma City rights. No exercise or complete comparison tree for those swaps is claimed here.

transactions.title: Oladipo moves again.
transactions.text: Miami acquires Oladipo. Houston receives Olynyk, Bradley and a conditional swap involving a pick it may hold from Brooklyn.

transactions.title: The extra Dallas first moves again.
transactions.text: Reddish joins Hill, cash and a Brooklyn second on the way to New York. Atlanta receives Knox and a protected Charlotte first.

transactions.title: LeVert becomes three draft paths.
transactions.text: Cleveland adds LeVert and a Miami second. Indiana receives Rubio, a protected first and two seconds.
notes: February 7 is the official acquisition announcement. The teams agreed to the exchange on February 6.

transactions.title: Hart leaves the Davis branch.
transactions.text: Portland sends McCollum, Nance and Snell to New Orleans. Hart joins three players and draft consideration heading west.

transactions.title: Indiana’s other branch goes west.
transactions.text: Sabonis joins Lamb, Justin Holiday and a second-round entitlement. Indiana acquires Haliburton, Hield and Thompson.

transactions.title: Thirteen months later, another exchange.
transactions.text: Harden and Millsap head to Philadelphia. Brooklyn receives Simmons, Curry, Drummond and two first-round obligations.
notes: The 2022/23 choice is a deferral option on one obligation, not two draft picks. The protected later first has a separate fallback.

transactions.title: The extra pick becomes part of another bet.
transactions.shortTitle: Langford joins the Derrick White package
transactions.text: Langford joins Richardson, a first and a swap right. Boston acquires Derrick White; the complete package matters.

transactions.title: Another first survives the lottery.
transactions.text: Cleveland lands at No. 14. Indiana’s first-round entitlement remains protected and rolls to 2023.

resolutions.detail: No. 14 is inside the protected range. The same obligation rolls to Cleveland’s lottery-protected 2023 first.

transactions.title: Brooklyn chooses next year.
transactions.text: The Nets notify the league that they will pass on Philadelphia’s No. 23 and take its 2023 first instead.

resolutions.detail: Brooklyn exercises its option to defer the Philadelphia first from 2022 to 2023. This leaves the 2022 selection with Philadelphia.

transactions.title: No. 17: Tari Eason
transactions.text: The first outright Brooklyn obligation from the Harden package becomes Houston’s No. 17 selection.

transactions.title: No. 12: Jalen Williams
transactions.text: The Clippers’ 2022 first becomes No. 12. Oklahoma City selects Jalen Williams.

transactions.title: No. 31: Andrew Nembhard
transactions.text: Houston’s second, sent to Indiana in the LeVert deal, becomes No. 31 and Andrew Nembhard.

transactions.title: No. 25: Blake Wesley
transactions.text: Boston’s first conveys at No. 25. San Antonio selects Blake Wesley.

transactions.title: Before the Holiday package.
transactions.text: Boston acquires Brogdon for five players and a protected first. He will later be part of the separate exchange with Portland.

transactions.title: A Brooklyn pick reaches Utah.
transactions.shortTitle: Sexton joins the Donovan Mitchell package
transactions.text: Sexton joins Markkanen, Agbaji and five future draft rights in Cleveland’s package for Donovan Mitchell.
notes: Sexton was signed and traded. September 3 is Cleveland’s official completion date; Utah published its retrospective announcement September 8.
Three outright firsts are unprotected. Later swap amendments and future conveyances are not followed.

transactions.title: Dallas adds another headliner.
transactions.text: Irving and Morris arrive together. Brooklyn receives two players and three future picks. Morris later joins the Luka package.

transactions.title: The Luka and Davis branches meet.
transactions.text: Reddish reaches Portland in a four-team exchange that sends Hart to New York. Their paths began in different headline trades.
notes: Draft rights to Tomić, Diez and Dubljević are part of the exchange. All net destinations in the completed four-team package are retained.
Portland, Philadelphia and Charlotte created traded-player exceptions. Those are generated cap capacity, not assets that can be passed between franchises.
The 2027 composite entitlement is not equated with the isolated New Orleans second from the earlier McCollum trade; a comparison right and an individual pick are different assets.

transactions.title: Poeltl comes back.
transactions.text: Toronto reacquires the center it once sent away. San Antonio receives Birch and three pick obligations.

transactions.title: No. 23: Kris Murray
transactions.text: New York’s first clears lottery protection. Portland selects Kris Murray at No. 23.

transactions.title: No. 26: Ben Sheppard
transactions.text: One draft later, Cleveland’s obligation conveys at No. 26. Indiana selects Ben Sheppard.

transactions.title: Dame time changes time zones.
transactions.text: Milwaukee gets Lillard. Portland receives Holiday, Ayton, Camara and future rights; Phoenix takes four players.

transactions.title: Four days in Portland.
transactions.text: Holiday is traded again before playing for Portland. Boston sends two players and two first-round obligations.

transactions.title: Another New York connection.
transactions.text: Anunoby joins the Knicks with Achiuwa and Flynn. Toronto receives Barrett, Quickley and Detroit’s next second.

transactions.title: No. 8: Rob Dillingham
transactions.text: Toronto’s first conveys at No. 8. San Antonio selects Dillingham before sending his rights to Minnesota.

transactions.title: No. 3: Reed Sheppard
transactions.text: Brooklyn’s next outright first becomes No. 3. Houston selects Reed Sheppard.

transactions.title: The eighth pick becomes more time.
transactions.text: Minnesota acquires Dillingham’s rights. San Antonio receives a distant first-round pick and a protected swap right.

transactions.title: No. 31: Jonathan Mogbo
transactions.text: Detroit’s second is the first selection of round two. Toronto uses No. 31 on Jonathan Mogbo.

transactions.title: A new center of gravity.
transactions.text: Towns heads to New York. Minnesota gets three players and a protected first; Charlotte supplies draft rights and takes players, picks and cash.
notes: Charlie Brown Jr., DaQuan Jeffries and Duane Washington Jr. were signed and traded. The Charlotte leg is part of this transaction.

transactions.title: The night nobody saw coming.
transactions.text: Luka changes teams again. Dallas receives Davis, Christie and a future first; Utah is the third team in the exchange.
notes: Cash from Utah facilitates the exchange; amounts are not asserted here. No later use of the 2025 seconds is traced in this story.

transactions.title: One headline. Five teams.
transactions.text: Butler goes to Golden State. Follow the entire exchange to see why Miami, Utah, Detroit and Toronto all appear in the same frame.
notes: This scene records net transfers in the completed five-team package; Schröder was routed through Utah. Martin had arrived in Detroit in a separate Philadelphia deal, outside this story.
Some minor second-round terms were not disclosed. Their announced consideration is retained, clearly labelled, with no invented origins or outcomes.

transactions.title: No. 17: Joan Beringer
transactions.text: Detroit’s first clears its top-13 protection. Minnesota uses No. 17 on Joan Beringer.

transactions.title: No. 20: Kasparas Jakučionis
transactions.text: The Golden State first conveys at No. 20. Miami selects Kasparas Jakučionis.

transactions.title: Washington enters the thread.
transactions.text: McCollum moves to Washington in a three-team package. Chicago’s 2027 second also arrives—and later joins the Davis return to Dallas.
notes: The final July 6 package includes Houston and Mojave King’s draft rights; the initial two-team report is incomplete.

transactions.title: A second arrival in Portland.
transactions.text: Portland reacquires Holiday for Simons. The completed deal is a player-for-player exchange; the draft picks in earlier reports were removed.

transactions.title: Atlanta’s path turns toward D.C.
transactions.text: The other player from draft night leaves Atlanta. Washington sends back two players; no draft pick is included.

transactions.title: Different paths. Same destination.
transactions.text: Davis follows Trae to Washington through a separate trade. The two branches meet in a city neither started in.
notes: The final three-team structure is recorded. The 2026 entitlement compares Oklahoma City, Houston and the Clippers. Coverage ends February 5, before the draft.

stories.title: The Luka ripple
stories.headline:
TWO PICKS.
TWO FUTURES.
stories.subtitle: A draft-night exchange. Two careers. An afterlife nobody could have drawn up.
stories.coverage: Traces Luka, Trae and the Dallas first through Reddish; the Reddish–Hart exchange joins the 2019 Davis branch. Follows New York’s first to Kris Murray and McCollum into Washington’s 2026 Trae exchange. Stops February 5, 2026. Other pick rights and secondary player branches are untraced.
stories.takeaway: The draft-night package opens several paths. Follow one asset at a time.
stories.imageAlt: Luka Dončić playing for Dallas in 2021

stories.title: The night Dallas changed
stories.headline:
ONE NIGHT.
TWO CORNERSTONES.
stories.subtitle: Dirk’s draft rights. Garrity’s next stop. The separate deal that brought Nash.
stories.coverage: Follows the separate Dirk and Nash draft-night packages, Dallas’s 1999 first to Marion, and Marion through Miami and Toronto back to Dallas in July 2009. Shaq’s Miami, Phoenix and Cleveland exchanges are shared intersections. Conditional Toronto picks and other branches stop at their recorded transfers; Nash’s free agency is not a trade return.
stories.takeaway: Pat Garrity’s rights connect the two deals. Each package still matters.
stories.imageAlt: Dirk Nowitzki playing for Dallas in 2009

stories.title: Brooklyn buys the present
stories.headline:
THE LONG
GAME.
stories.subtitle: Three firsts, one swap, and the patience between a promise and a player.
stories.coverage: Follows the Brooklyn picks to Young, Brown, the Tatum trade-down, Sexton’s Donovan Mitchell package, and Langford’s Derrick White package through September 3, 2022. White’s 2022 first becomes Blake Wesley. Other player moves, later swap amendments and future picks are untraced.
stories.takeaway: A swap is a right to exchange picks. Boston still needed another trade to reach No. 3.
stories.imageAlt: Kevin Garnett playing for Boston in 2008

stories.title: Thirteen to Los Angeles
stories.headline:
BEFORE
THE LEGEND.
stories.subtitle: A draft selection in Charlotte. A rights transfer two weeks later.
stories.coverage: The June 26 selection and July 11, 1996 Bryant–Divac exchange only. This is a short origin story; later free agency is outside the trade graph.
stories.takeaway: Draft night and the effective trade date are not always the same day.

stories.title: The dynasty splits
stories.headline:
THE BIG
AFTERLIFE.
stories.subtitle: From Shaq’s move to Miami to two very different Gasol destinations.
stories.coverage: Follows both Shaq pick returns, Marion’s Dallas route, Butler’s Dallas exchange, the Gasol packages, and the Lakers 2010 first through Vásquez to Powell rights, Anunoby and Mogbo. Stops June 27, 2024. Untraced obligations are labelled; no free agency or shared championship is treated as a trade connection.
stories.takeaway: The connection runs through whole packages, with additional assets entering each time.

stories.title: The brothers in the fine print
stories.headline:
A TALE OF
TWO GASOLS.
stories.subtitle: One brother headlines the trade. The other appears as draft rights.
stories.coverage: Follows Marc to Toronto and the Lakers 2010 first to Vásquez, then his New Orleans, Sacramento, Toronto and Milwaukee exchanges. The Clippers first becomes Anunoby; the later Knicks package’s Detroit second becomes Mogbo. Stops June 27, 2024. The Lakers 2008 first and other side branches remain untraced.
stories.takeaway: A draft-rights entry in one deal can become the headliner of another.

stories.title: Boston’s two big swings
stories.headline:
ALL IN.
THEN RESET.
stories.subtitle: The 2007 arrival and the 2013 departure belong to different Boston bets.
stories.coverage: Follows the Brooklyn picks to Young, Brown, the Tatum trade-down, Sexton’s Donovan Mitchell package, and Langford’s Derrick White package through September 3, 2022. White’s 2022 first becomes Blake Wesley. Other player moves, later swap amendments and future picks are untraced.
stories.takeaway: Returning a team’s own pick obligation extinguishes a claim; it creates no extra pick.
stories.imageAlt: Kevin Garnett playing for Boston in 2008

stories.title: Houston finds its headliner
stories.headline:
THE BET
ON THIRTEEN.
stories.subtitle: The player went to Houston. Three very different draft promises went the other way.
stories.coverage: From Houston’s 2012 acquisition through the completed 2021 four-team exchange and 2022 Philadelphia deal. Selected pick branches become Adams, Abrines, McGary, Eason, Nembhard, Ben Sheppard and Reed Sheppard. Stops June 26, 2024; later player moves, swap amendments and unused fallback terms are untraced.
stories.takeaway: A protected pick can survive one draft and convey at the next. It is still one obligation.

stories.title: The return trip
stories.headline:
A LEAP.
A LOOP.
stories.subtitle: Kawhi goes north. Years later, Poeltl’s branch circles back to Toronto.
stories.coverage: Follows Keldon Johnson and Poeltl’s return, then Toronto’s No. 8 into the Dillingham rights trade. Stops June 26, 2024 with Minnesota’s future first and swap outstanding at that point.
stories.takeaway: A returning player can open a new branch years after the original exchange.

stories.title: The price of right now
stories.headline:
FIVE FIRSTS.
ONE FUTURE.
stories.subtitle: George arrives in Oklahoma City, then leaves in a very different kind of deal.
stories.coverage: Both sides of Indiana’s George return are followed: Sabonis into the Haliburton package; Oladipo through the four-team Harden deal, LeVert, Nembhard and Ben Sheppard. Includes the full Clippers package and Jalen Williams. Stops June 22, 2023; other picks and intervening free agency are untraced.
stories.takeaway: Shai and the draft obligations arrive in the same package. Their later paths remain distinct.

stories.title: The Davis chain
stories.headline:
THREE CITIES.
THREE DEALS.
stories.subtitle: New Orleans to Los Angeles. Dallas to Washington. Follow the actual packages.
stories.coverage: The Davis route from 2019 through February 2026, plus Hart into the Reddish exchange and New York’s first into Kris Murray. McCollum’s New Orleans–Washington–Atlanta path is included, as is Chicago’s second through Washington to Dallas. Other rights are untraced beyond their displayed transactions.
stories.takeaway: Washington appears in the first deal as a facilitator and in the last as Davis’s destination.

stories.title: Another Dallas crossroads
stories.headline:
TWO STARS.
MORE THREADS.
stories.subtitle: Kyrie’s arrival includes Markieff Morris. Follow the less obvious thread.
stories.coverage: Follows Morris from the Kyrie package into the Luka deal, then Davis into Washington. This is not a claim that Kyrie was traded for any of those returns. Brooklyn’s picks are untraced.
stories.takeaway: Shared teammates can connect trades whose headline players never change hands for one another.

stories.title: Four days in Portland
stories.headline:
THE HOLIDAY
DETOUR.
stories.subtitle: Dame moves to Milwaukee. Jrue’s Portland stop turns out to be very short.
stories.coverage: Includes Brogdon’s 2022 Boston arrival as backward context for the 2023 Holiday package, then Lillard’s three-team trade, Holiday to Boston and the July 7, 2025 Simons exchange. Future draft rights and other player branches are untraced.
stories.takeaway: The final 2025 exchange contains no draft picks; early reports described a different proposal.

stories.title: A new center of gravity
stories.headline:
BIG MAN.
BIGGER PACKAGE.
stories.subtitle: The New York–Minnesota headline has a Charlotte chapter, too.
stories.coverage: The complete October 2, 2024 three-team trade and Detroit’s first conveying to Minnesota as No. 17 in 2025. Other players and second-round outcomes are untraced.
stories.takeaway: The original franchise of a traded pick can be a team that did not participate in this deal.

stories.title: Five teams, one headline
stories.headline:
THE FIVE-TEAM
SHUFFLE.
stories.subtitle: A deadline blockbuster whose edges reach far beyond Miami and Golden State.
stories.coverage: The final February 6 five-team package and the Golden State first becoming Miami’s No. 20. Some minor second-round terms were undisclosed; those assets are labelled and left untraced.
stories.takeaway: A headline is an entry point. The full exchange is the story.
